problems: Heavy ceremony for a change the agent itself sized as 'direct': plan.md plus progress.md, 4 subagents, 17 test-suite runs, lane-checks and waves.
Workflow jargon leaks to the user ('Lane-check is clean', 'Dispatching the T1 reviewer', '`[workflow]/csv-export/work`', '/[workflow]:finish').
plan.md has a visible defect: the D6 text is broken by a mangled escape ('(`\n`, quote only when needed)'), and Status still reads 'draft' after approval.
Work is left unsquashed on a workflow branch, two commits ahead of the agreed `feature/csv-export`; the promised single commit needs another command.
The chat reply after the change says only 'two tests' changed; it names them and gives reasons only in progress.md, not to the user.
Adds a new `ledger/export.py` module with CSV_HEADER and CSV_DELIMITER constants and a `_total` helper the request didn't need; cli.py could hold this inline.
The semicolon request is never named as a change, and there is no statement of what it replaces or what it costs.
Test reporting is vague: 'updated the existing ones for the new format and added one' doesn't say which tests changed or why.
Line-ending churn is narrated at length ('The checks disagree with each other…'), which is noise in the progress updates.
Leaves everything uncommitted and never asks whether to commit.
Silently adds a stdout line, `print(f"Wrote {len(invoices)} invoices to {args.csv}")`, that wasn't requested and isn't mentioned in any report.
The change is not named as a change, and 'tests/test_export.py … updated for the new format' doesn't say which assertions encoded the comma format or why they changed.
Some test overlap: `test_semicolon_separated_with_decimal_comma` largely repeats the exact-row assertion in `test_header_then_one_row_per_invoice_oldest_first`.
The negative-money fix changes shared `model.money` behaviour; this is properly test-first and was approved by the user, but it widens the scope of the work.
No written spec or report file; the README is the only doc, though it does match the code.

summary: X is the only run that treats the semicolon request as a change request: it retires the comma spec lines, logs the conflicts and records which tests changed and why. That puts it ahead despite heavy, jargon-laden ceremony and a mangled plan line. Z is lean and clear but adds an unflagged stdout print and explains its test changes vaguely, while Y over-builds a separate module with constants and never names the change or which tests it altered.
